newsitem.title: USA: GASB finalizes muni fair market value standards.
newsitem.headline: GASB finalizes muni fair market value standards.

text.p: The Government Accounting Standards Board (GASB) gave final approval to a controversial standard requiring municipalities to value the equities and debt in their investment portfolios at their current market value, GASB said.

Up until now, municipalities claiming to follow generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) were allowed to value their portfolios at the price they originally paid for the investments, GASB said.

But with localities investing more and more in sophisticated and volatile instruments like derivative products, GASB said it is time for governments to give investors a more current picture of their financial holdings.

State treasurers had opposed the new standard, which GASB has been developing for the last year. They said in comments last year that current value reporting would give investors only a snapshot of portfolio values and could confuse investors.
